name: MOTIVE
aliases: Male Overactive Bladder Treatment in Veterans
question: In men with persistent overactive bladder symptoms after alpha-blocker treatment, is behavioral therapy equivalent to adding oxybutynin extended release for daily voiding frequency?

arms.label: Behavioral therapy added to alpha-blocker treatment
oxybutynin extended release added to alpha-blocker treatment

design.population: Men aged 42–88 years without bladder outlet obstruction who still had urgency and more than eight daily voids after a four-week alpha-blocker run-in.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Objectives, Design, Participants, Interventions

verdictNote: The prespecified equivalence analysis found equivalent posttreatment daily voiding means.
takeaway: In men with persistent overactive bladder symptoms after alpha-blocker treatment, eight weeks of behavioral therapy and titrated oxybutynin extended release produced equivalent posttreatment daily voiding frequency (9.1 versus 9.5 voids/day; equivalence P < .01).

reports.label: Primary equivalence report
reports.citation: Burgio KL, Goode PS, Johnson TM, et al. "Behavioral Versus Drug Treatment for Overactive Bladder in Men: The Male Overactive Bladder Treatment in Veterans (MOTIVE) Trial." *J Am Geriatr Soc.* 2011;59(12):2209-2216. doi:10.1111/j.1532-5415.2011.03724.x
reports.followUp: Eight weeks of randomized treatment after a four-week alpha-blocker run-in

results.measure: Mean voids per 24 hours after eight weeks; equivalence test
results.note: The abstract reports equivalent posttreatment means but does not give the equivalence margin, arm denominators or confidence interval.

results.measure: Mean change in nightly episodes after eight weeks
Mean change in maximum urgency score after eight weeks

delivery.label: Behavioral treatment
delivery.value: Pelvic floor muscle exercises, urge suppression techniques and delayed voiding for eight weeks, added after a four-week alpha-blocker run-in.

delivery.label: Drug treatment
delivery.value: Individually titrated oxybutynin extended release, 5–30 mg/day for eight weeks, added after a four-week alpha-blocker run-in.

reports.label: Nocturia analysis
reports.citation: Johnson TM 2nd, Markland AD, Goode PS, et al. "Efficacy of Adding Behavioural Treatment or Antimuscarinic Drug Therapy to α-Blocker Therapy in Men with Nocturia." *BJU Int.* 2013;112(1):100-108. doi:10.1111/j.1464-410X.2012.11736.x
reports.followUp: Nocturia analysis after the randomized treatment period
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Patients and methods; primary report abstract, Interventions

results.endpoint: Nocturia in men with at least one baseline nightly episode
results.measure: Mean reduction in nightly episodes among 127 men
results.note: The abstract gives the combined analysis population but not arm denominators.

results.endpoint: Nocturia in men with at least two baseline nightly episodes
results.measure: Mean reduction in nightly episodes among 76 men
results.note: The abstract gives the combined analysis population but not arm denominators.
